text:
Maria (PM): quick sync — we need a concrete decision on the traffic-shaping + backfill playbook for Dedicated launch. two approaches on the table: conservative cushion per pool (20% headroom) + opportunistic backfill OR tenant-level smoothing (per-tenant token bands + short-term burst leases). i prefer hybrid. thoughts?

Alex (Eng): high-level: hybrid seems safest. reserve headroom to satisfy SLOs, use backfill only for non-SLA traffic. question: how do we mark traffic as eligible for backfill? tag at route-level? customer opt-in?

Maria (PM): route-level flag + customer opt-in for backfill makes sense. defaults: critical routes block backfill. non-critical routes eligible. policy config lives in Dedicated pool config.

Tyler (Runtime): runtime constraints: backfill needs fast preempt + graceful eviction. KV caches and prefix caches must survive short preemption windows or rehydrate quickly. if we evict active allocations aggressively, p99 jumps.

Sophia (SRE): +1. must have metrics and playbook: p50/p95/p99 latency, eviction rate, cache-miss after preempt, queue length, backfill fill-rate. alerting thresholds: preempt_rate > 2% in 5m -> paging.

Kevin (Sales): customers asking for predictable burst. they'll tolerate backfill only if billing and SLAs are clear. need explicit checkbox in onboarding, docs and a visible "backfill usage" metric in Console for transparency. also need guidance on pricing discounts when backfill used.

Lisa (Onboarding): agree — onboarding checklist item: opt-in flag, sample config, expected impact. also need runbook for customers to opt-out quickly during incidents.

Alex (Eng): proposal for policy element (config sample):
```
pool_policy:
  cushion_pct: 20            # reserved capacity buffer
  eligible_backfill: ["low-priority", "async"]
  preempt_mode: "opportunistic"
  spill_policy: "throttle"      # how to shape spillover to other pools
  tenant_burst_bands:
    enabled: true
    bucket_seconds: 300
    max_burst: 3x
```

Tyler (Runtime): notes on implementation:
- preempt_mode=opportunistic -> use spot-style nodes or lower-priority workers. fallback chain: same-model-quantized -> smaller context model -> abort with helpful error.
- need KV cache checkpointing to avoid full re-warm on preempt.

Sophia (SRE): monitoring roadmap:
- Console dashboard: "Backfill Fill %", "Cushion Utilization", "Tenant Burst Usage"
- Canary: enable backfill in us-west for 2 pilot customers for 48h, track all metrics.

Maria (PM): launch criteria (beta):
- pilot with 2 customers for 48h with no >1% increase in p99 latency across pool
- backfill transparency in Console + billing note
- documented opt-out and incident-runbook
- automated fallback chain implemented (model variants or meaningful error)

Kevin (Sales): commercial ask: pilot customers want a SLA carveout doc. I can draft a short addendum if engineering OK with wording: "backfill may use opportunistic capacity; critical traffic remains protected."

Alex (Eng): technical tradeoffs / risks:
- risk A: cache rewarm causes latency spike after eviction. mitigation: keep small warm spare per pool or checkpointing.
- risk B: billing complexity. mitigation: show backfill usage per route and monthly caps.

Lisa (Onboarding): runbook snippet for customers to opt-out quickly:
"Settings -> Dedicated Pool -> Traffic shaping -> Backfill = Off" + API: POST /pool/:id/config {"eligible_backfill": []}

ops-bot: deploy pipeline report: nightly-build passed for backfill-proto branch (CI 8642). staging deploy scheduled.

Sophia (SRE): ops runbook for incidents:
- If p99 > target after backfill enabled: set pool_policy.cushion_pct=40 (increase headroom)
- If preempt_rate spikes: disable eligible_backfill for affected pool
- If cache-miss rate > threshold: spin warm spare node and prioritize rehydrate

Maria (PM): decided next steps / owners:
- Alex -> prototype config + API for route-level flags (ETA: 1 week)
- Tyler -> runtime preempt fallback design + KV checkpoint plan (ETA: 2 weeks)
- Sophia -> dashboard + alert definitions (ETA: 1 week)
- Kevin -> draft SLA carveout and pricing language (ETA: 3 days)
- Lisa -> onboarding copy + opt-out flow doc (ETA: 3 days)

Alex (Eng): SGTM. I'll create a short RFC and attach config example + test plan.

Kevin (Sales): I'll loop in pilot customers, ask for permission to run 48h test, will get back by EOD.

Maria (PM): ok — let's keep this thread for decisions. if any blockers surface ping @Maria. thanks all :thumbsup:

Alex (Eng): one more q: do we want to expose cushion_pct to customers or keep it internal?

Kevin (Sales): customers want visibility but probably not control initially. expose read-only in Console, control by support for GA.

Maria (PM): agreed. read-only for beta. revisit GA.

Sophia (SRE): noted. I'll add that to dashboard mockups.

Maria (PM): closing notes: this playbook aims to balance predictable SLA-backed capacity with lower-cost opportunistic fill. keep the pilot narrow and measurable. will sync in 3 days for check-in.
